context: Checks whether the final artifact follows the apply-stack-conventions instructions from the published Rails Agent Skills tile.

checklist.name: instruction-1
checklist.description: The submitted artifact follows this skill instruction: ALL new code MUST have its test written and validated BEFORE implementation.

checklist.name: instruction-2
checklist.description: The submitted artifact follows this skill instruction: Write the spec file content, not only the spec path: bundle exec rspec spec/[path]_spec.rb

checklist.name: instruction-3
checklist.description: The submitted artifact follows this skill instruction: Verify it FAILS — output must show the observed failure proving the feature does not exist yet

checklist.name: instruction-4
checklist.description: The submitted artifact follows this skill instruction: Write the implementation code

checklist.name: instruction-5
checklist.description: The submitted artifact follows this skill instruction: Verify it PASSES — run the same spec and include the observed green result line

checklist.name: instruction-6
checklist.description: The submitted artifact follows this skill instruction: The final artifact must show the test proof before implementation code.

checklist.name: instruction-7
checklist.description: The submitted artifact follows this skill instruction: Use **Observed RED output** and **Observed GREEN output** labels for proof

checklist.name: instruction-8
checklist.description: The submitted artifact follows this skill instruction: Each step should remain testable in isolation before wiring to the next layer.

checklist.name: instruction-9
checklist.description: The submitted artifact follows this skill instruction: When applying stack conventions, your output MUST include:

checklist.name: instruction-10
checklist.description: The submitted artifact follows this skill instruction: **Tests-first proof before implementation** — Put this section before any implementation code. For each layer, include the actual spec code written or updated, the exact command (`bundle exec rspec spec/[path]_spec.rb`), and the **Observed RED output** proving the feature is absent rather than misconfigured. Do not use placeholder or illustrative `e.g.` failure lines.
